questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Experience life in a different city and meet people from different places.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, the exchange office send out every needed piece of information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The introduction days helped us fill out any needed documents.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Very nice place. Cheaper than anything else I saw in Amsterdam. A bit outside the city, but very close to uni, and the other people on exchange.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Shared kitchen

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I recommend it, it’s a good way to meet everyone. Especially in the introduction days, and the rooms are fine.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You register for courses, and your vu-profile. It’s very easy and you get several reminders and guides for how to do it.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Exchange Office answered any question I had about the process.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: There were some courses I wanted that were too popular for them to let exchange students choose them. I wasn’t aware of this before, so it was a but unfortunate. I was able to get other courses though.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware that you have to be very flexible in your choices. A minor is definetely easier when it comes to planning, but it’s also possible to make your own. It just requires a bit more planning.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A lot more group works, and a different kind of lectures compared to KU. The lectures had more engagement compared to KU.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Easier

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Above

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Challenges in Global Health, Key strategies in disability and neuropathies, Brian in trouble, Developing brain, Mind and Machine.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Key strategies in disability and neuropathies. Very interesting lectures if you’re interested in how society fits and excludes people of different abilities.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Public transportation is very expensive. I biked almost everywhere, so 200 is very low bc I didn’t use it a lot.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: About the same as in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The Sportscenter is good for joining classes.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The ESN hosted several social activities. The VU introduced us to the sportscenter and a city day for exploring Amsterdam.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I highly recommend going to all the introductory days. It’s these days you will meet everyone and have the easiest time socializing.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on weekend trips/ day trips outside Amsterdam. It’s nice to get a out and see the other cities nearby.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Only met them in classes and group works.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Very similar to danish culture. The local food was very bland though, so that I dont recommend.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Friendly people, very helpful.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Go to the introductory days, live at uilenstede, and be open to all the new experiences.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remember to book the tickets for the introductory days and the seperate ticket for the intro-party. They don’t have unlimited tickets so book it early. They send out info for when to do this.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the people I met.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It can be a bit tiring too meet so many people in the beginning. But it doesn’t last forever, so just be ready to have the same conversations a lot of times in the beginning. It’s also fun though, just can be a bit tiring.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
